newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end sharply higher, boosted by bonds.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end sharply higher, boosted by bonds.

text.p: Madrid stock indices ended bourse trade sharply higher on Tuesday, boosted by gains in Wall Street and other European bourses and after stocks tracked a surge in Spanish bonds, traders said.
The general index closed 4.35 points, 1.16 percent, up at 380.69. The Ibex-35 climbed 57.23 points, 1.33 percent, to close at 4,373.87.
Traders said bullish sentiment on Wall Street ahead of U.S. presidential elections had boosted the Spanish bourse along with most other European stock markets.
"Strength in bonds amid expectations that interest rates in Europe will remain favourable have boosted stocks, and we should see more gains in the coming days," said one trader.
Dealers said it was possible stocks could break higher and conquer new historic highs in the following sessions.
Telefonica and electricity stocks proved to be the best performers of the day. Telefonica rose 55 pesetas to 2,600. Endesa gained 130 pesetas to 8,000.
The banking sector delivered more moderate gains. Santander rose 160 pesetas to 6,720.
